question: Who among the following was the deputy chairman of Planning Commission under the tenth five year plan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**K.C. Pant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **K.C. Pant** served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India during the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007).
 
• He was a seasoned politician and a prominent member of the Indian National Congress, later joining the Bharatiya Janata Party.
 
• The Tenth Five Year Plan emphasized **poverty reduction, employment generation, and improving human development indicators** such as education and health.
 
• Under K.C. Pant’s leadership, the Planning Commission worked towards achieving a targeted GDP growth rate of 8% during the plan period.
 
• He played a significant role in formulating policies related to economic reforms and development during his tenure at the Planning Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shankarrao Chavan**
 
 
• Shankarrao Chavan was a senior politician from the Indian National Congress who served as the **Chief Minister of Maharashtra** twice and held key Union Cabinet positions, including Home Minister and Finance Minister.
 
• He was not associated with the Planning Commission as Deputy Chairman during the Tenth Five Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **Yashwant Sinha**
 
 
• Yashwant Sinha is an Indian politician and former civil servant who served as the **Finance Minister of India from 1990-1991 and 1998-2002**.
 
• Although he played a critical role in economic reforms during his tenure, he was not associated with the Planning Commission as Deputy Chairman during the Tenth Five Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **P. Shiv Shankar**
 
 
• P. Shiv Shankar was a senior Congress leader and held various portfolios in the Union Cabinet, such as Law and Justice, External Affairs, and Human Resource Development.
 
• However, he was not associated with the Planning Commission during the Tenth Five Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission and the Tenth Five Year Plan**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India that formulated India’s Five Year Plans, among other functions, to promote a balanced and planned development of the economy.
 
• The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002–2007) focused on **doubling per capita income in 10 years** and achieving a **poverty ratio reduction by 5 percentage points** by 2007.
 
• The plan aimed at promoting inclusive growth, improving infrastructure, and fostering sustainable development.
